newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka closes oil storage repair tender Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka closes oil storage repair tender Sept 18.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) will close tenders for rebuilding its damaged oil storage tanks on Wednesday, company officials said on Monday.
The tenders for a turnkey contract only require qualifications of bidders and CPC will invite techinical proposals from a selected group, they said.

The contract is to repair five of 11 damaged tanks in Kolonnawa and both the damaged tanks in Orugodawatta, in the suburbs of Colombo. The tanks were damaged in attacks last year by Tamil Tiger rebels.
The Sri Lankan government has secured a loan of about 2.5 billion rupees from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to rebuild all the damaged tanks.
CPC Chairman Anil Obeysekera told Reuters earlier this month the decision on the tender winner would probably be made in the first quarter of 1997.
